title: Hom from a perfect source commutes with affine inverse limits of spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves and canonical tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived pullback $Lh^*$ is computed by K-flat resolutions with flat terms and $Rh_*$ by K-injective resolutions. A perfect object means one etale locally isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(X_i,q_{ji})$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $S$ with affine transition morphisms, and $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ with projections $q_i$. Quasi-compact means that the space admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; quasi-separated means its diagonal is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. An affine morphism is representable with affine inverse images of affine scheme tests. Fix $i\in I$, a perfect $P_i\in D(\mathcal O_{X_i})$, and any $K_i\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X_i})$, with no boundedness or finite Tor dimension assumption on $K_i$. Put $P_j=Lq_{ji}^*P_i$, $K_j=Lq_{ji}^*K_i$, $P=Lq_i^*P_i$, and $K=Lq_i^*K_i$. The canonical pullback-induced map $$\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{X_j})}(P_j,K_j)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(P,K)$$ is bijective. Transition maps use the canonical composition isomorphisms of derived pullback.

proof.text: Pass to the tail $j\ge i$, which is still small and directed. For every qcqs etale $t:T\to X_i$ set $T_j=T\times_{X_i}X_j$ and $T_\infty=T\times_{X_i}X$. The affine-limit and affine-locality lemmas identify $T_\infty=\varprojlim_{j\ge i}T_j$, give affine projections and transitions, and show the $T_j$ are qcqs. Pullback to $T$ and then to $T_j$ agrees with restriction of $P_j,K_j$ by the etale chart calculus, including its composition comparisons; $K_j|_{T_j}$ remains quasi-coherent in cohomology. Define $\mathcal C(T)$ to mean that the pullback-induced Hom comparison for these restrictions is bijective with $K_i|_T$ replaced by $K_i|_T[n]$ for every integer $n$. This simultaneous formulation supplies both adjacent degrees needed in excision. Restriction of a local bounded finite-free summand model remains such a model, so $P_i|_T$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 09RI (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), first paragraph, property P; strengthened to all shifts. Tags 07SF and 08GP for the limit and induction setup.

proof.text: Suppose $T$ is affine. Then all $T_j$ and $T_\infty$ are affine schemes by affine locality and the affine projections. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, $T_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$, $T_\infty=\operatorname{Spec}A$; limit sections gives $A=\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}A_j$ with its actual transition maps. The perfect object's cohomology is quasi-coherent by the qc-space perfectness lemma. Thus the unbounded Zariski–etale equivalence applies to both restricted objects. Etale detection of perfectness makes the Zariski preimage of $P_i|_T$ perfect. The affine perfect-model theorem supplies a bounded finite-projective $A_0$-complex $B^\bullet$ representing it. The affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence gives an arbitrary $A_0$-complex representing the preimage of $K_i|_T$; choose a flat-term K-flat replacement $C^\bullet$ by the module-resolution theorem. Neither equivalence nor this resolution requires a cohomological bound on $K_i$.

source.place: Tag 09RI, affine paragraph; Tag 09RE (perfect.tex, lemma-descend-homomorphisms), case (1); Tags 071Q and 08HG for comparison and perfection.

proof.text: For $D=A_j$ or $A$, affine derived pullback identifies the two pulled-back objects with the etale realizations of $B^\bullet\otimes_{A_0}D$ and $C^\bullet\otimes_{A_0}D$. For the first model each term is a summand of a finite free module, so its tensor functor is a summand of a finite sum of the exact identity functor and is exact; the bounded-flat K-flatness lemma then shows ordinary tensor computes derived tensor; for the second this follows from K-flatness. A finite-projective term is a summand of a finite free module, and tensoring its splitting shows that the first model is again bounded finite-projective. Since both pulled-back objects have quasi-coherent cohomology, the Zariski–etale equivalence (between full subcategories) and the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence for $D$ identify their etale derived Hom groups with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(D)}$ between these two module complexes. Bounded-above projectivity and the K-projective localization bijection therefore identify these derived maps with chain maps modulo homotopy. Chain-level extension/restriction of scalars sends a map $a$ to $b\mapsto a(b\otimes1)$, with inverse $v\mapsto(b\otimes d\mapsto d\,v(b))$; these formulas also send homotopies to homotopies. Consequently the Hom group at $D$ in degree $n$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_0)}(B^\bullet,(C^\bullet\otimes_{A_0}D)[n])$. All transition and limit maps become $v\mapsto(1\otimes\alpha)\circ v$: the displayed formulas commute with iterated scalar extension, and the Zariski–etale pullback comparison respects composition.

source.place: Tag 09RE, case (1), the passage from derived maps after scalar extension to homotopy maps over the initial ring.

proof.text: The colimit $A$ of the $A_0$-algebras is also their colimit as $A_0$-modules. Tensor-colimit preservation with each $C^r$ gives $\operatorname{colim}_j(C^r\otimes_{A_0}A_j)=C^r\otimes_{A_0}A$, naturally for the differentials. Thus $N_j^\bullet=C^\bullet\otimes_{A_0}A_j$ has degreewise colimit $N^\bullet=C^\bullet\otimes_{A_0}A$. This assertion uses no flatness of the transition rings.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), case (1), final finite-projective homotopy-category calculation, with finite generators and equations written explicitly.

proof.text: Here is the finite-coordinate argument for the comparison $\operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_0)}(B^\bullet,N_j^\bullet[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_0)}(B^\bullet,N^\bullet[n])$. Choose splittings $u_r:B^r\to A_0^{m_r}$ and $v_r:A_0^{m_r}\to B^r$ with $v_ru_r=1$ for the finitely many nonzero terms. For any module map $f:B^r\to N^s$, lift the finitely many values $f(v_r(e_a))$ to one stage by the elementwise colimit criterion. The resulting map $g:A_0^{m_r}\to N_j^s$ gives a lift $g u_r$ of $f$, since its limit image is $f v_r u_r=f$. Likewise two maps with source $B^r$ whose limit images agree agree at a later stage: apply eventual equality to their values on the finite generating list $v_r(e_a)$. Finite lists of such maps or equalities can be treated at a single stage by directedness.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), case (1), final finite-projective homotopy-category calculation, with finite generators and equations written explicitly.

proof.text: Given a chain map $f:B^\bullet\to N^\bullet[n]$, lift its finitely many components by the preceding construction. The defects $d g^r-g^{r+1}d$ vanish in the colimit, and there are only finitely many nonzero possible defects because $B$ is bounded. Eventual equality, applied to each defect on its finite generating list, kills them at one later stage. The resulting chain map lifts $f$, proving surjectivity on homotopy classes. For injectivity, bring two representatives to a common stage and let $h^r:B^r\to N^{r+n-1}$ be a homotopy between their limit maps, using the shifted target differential. Lift the finitely many $h^r$. The finitely many equations $f-g=dh+hd$ hold after passing to a later stage by the same finite-generator test. Hence the representatives become homotopic there. This proves the desired bijection for every $n$. Under step 3 it is precisely the pullback Hom comparison, so $\mathcal C(T)$ holds for all affine $T$, including the empty affine, whose complexes and Hom groups are zero.

source.place: Tag 09RE (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), case (1), final finite-projective homotopy-category calculation, with finite generators and equations written explicitly.

proof.text:
Let $(U\subset W,V\to W)$ be a square in the distinguished-square induction principle, and put $T=U\times_WV$. Base change gives distinguished squares at each $j$ and at infinity. Apply the derived-Hom Mayer–Vietoris lemma to the restrictions of $P_j,K_j$ on each $W_j$ and at infinity. Its boundary naturality makes these long exact sequences a directed system and makes the pullback comparisons a morphism from its colimit to the limit sequence. Filtered colimits of abelian groups preserve exactness, so the source row is exact; the colimit of the two local summands is the sum of their colimits, by the finite biproduct universal property. With $A^n_Z=\operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Hom}(P_j|_{Z_j},K_j|_{Z_j}[n])$ and $B^n_Z$ the corresponding Hom group at infinity, we obtain the commutative exact five-term diagram
$$ A_U^{n-1}\oplus A_V^{n-1}\to A_T^{n-1}\to A_W^n\to A_U^n\oplus A_V^n\to A_T^n $$
over the same row with $B$ in place of $A$. If $\mathcal C(U),\mathcal C(V),\mathcal C(T)$ hold, its four outer vertical arrows are bijections.

source.place: Tag 09RI, first paragraph, condition (2) via Tag 08H9; filtered exactness is applied to Hom groups, not to an unbounded cohomology spectral sequence.

proof.text: Here is the diagram chase for the middle comparison. For surjectivity, take $y\in B_W^n$, lift its image in $B_U^n\oplus B_V^n$ to $a$ in the upper local pair. Its obstruction in $A_T^n$ is zero by injectivity of that comparison, so exactness lifts $a$ to $x\in A_W^n$. The difference $y-\bar x$ comes from $B_T^{n-1}$; lift that element to $A_T^{n-1}$ and add its boundary to $x$. For injectivity, if $x\in A_W^n$ has zero lower image, its local image is zero by the local-pair bijection, hence $x=\partial t$. The lower image of $t$ comes from $B_U^{n-1}\oplus B_V^{n-1}$. Lift that pair to the upper row and subtract its image from $t$; injectivity at $A_T^{n-1}$ then makes the difference zero. Thus $x=0$. This proves $\mathcal C(W)$ for every $n$.

source.place: Tag 09RI, the elementary exact-sequence chase behind condition (2).

proof.text: The property $\mathcal C$ is invariant under isomorphism over $X_i$, since every map defining it is canonical derived pullback. The affine case and the distinguished-square step verify exactly hypotheses (a) and (b) of the qcqs-space induction principle. Apply it with base $X_i$ to obtain $\mathcal C(X_i)$. Its clause $n=0$ is the asserted bijection. The maps are the prescribed pullback-induced maps, as checked on the affine models and in the base-change naturality of Mayer–Vietoris; no choice of model changes that cocone.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09RI (lemma-descend-homomorphisms), clause (1), proof using Tag 08GP, Tag 08H9, and the affine calculation in perfect.tex Tag 09RE (1).
